correctness.rationale: For each fixed n>=2 the eight Bernoulli row patterns partition into six distinct integer base levels; only the two duplicated levels produce nonconstant fitted coefficients when all base levels agree. Their exact multinomial event probabilities are A_n and B_n. On these events the fitted slope is 1+1/sqrt(epsilon), exact centered errors are -1/(3sqrt(epsilon)) and -4/(3sqrt(epsilon)), and the corrected Gram is eventually negative. Every complementary ensemble yields bounded error and eventually nonnegative output by the finite-state trichotomy. This proves the 1/epsilon MSE leading coefficient and limiting negativity probability with all quantifiers and boundaries. A deterministic coefficient 1 gives exact risk 2epsilon/(9n) and a positive corrected Gram. Exact-rational finite checks for n=2,3,4 supplement, not substitute for, the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The main 2026 finite-element projected Gram sketch proposes empirical control-variate weights and motivates variance reduction and preserving positive-definite matrix geometry. An exact positive-probability deterioration and an unbounded risk ratio, despite bounded SPD coefficients and vanishing control mismatch, identify a genuine parameter-conditioning and coefficient-estimation risk in a natural implementation. The theorem separates dangerous adaptive weights from safe known weights, motivates clipping/pilot estimation without claiming those remedies, and supplies sharp reproducible finite-ensemble benchmarks rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
